theses.title: Where hyperscaler capex actually lands
theses.standfirst: Every AI-datacenter dollar the hyperscalers spend is captured somewhere along a chain of suppliers. This map shows the realized split — each layer's and each company's share of the AI-revenue landing today, weighted by how much of its business depends on that spend. Descriptive, not a forecast.

control.label: Hyperscaler capex growth, year over year

share_weights._note: AI-attributable fraction of trailing revenue by exposure band — a desk estimate, meant to be argued with.

market.note: Round estimates of combined hyperscaler (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta + others) AI-datacenter capex, as of mid-2026 — our read, meant to be argued with, not a precise figure.

layers.name: AI compute chips (GPUs & accelerators)
layers.lagText: Guide-quarter. Moves first, prices the whole chain.

names.note: Sets the pace for every layer below.
names.watch: Data-center revenue guide and Blackwell-class lead times.

names.note: Accelerator share is the swing factor.
names.watch: MI-series datacenter GPU run-rate vs guidance.

names.note: Custom silicon plus networking. Sits in two layers.
names.watch: AI/custom-ASIC revenue mix and hyperscaler bookings.

names.note: Custom ASIC and optical DSP. Straddles L1 and L4.
names.watch: Custom-silicon design-win commentary + optical DSP.

names.note: Capacity is the true upstream constraint.
names.watch: CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity and HPC revenue share.

layers.name: AI memory (HBM & DRAM)
layers.lagText: About one quarter behind. Contract-priced, so cyclical.

names.note: The listed HBM/DRAM proxy — datacenter memory demand drives the cycle.
names.watch: HBM bit-share and whether it's sold out forward.

names.note: Storage tier, later in the build order.
names.watch: Enterprise SSD pricing and datacenter storage demand.

layers.name: Optical interconnect
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Bandwidth demand converts to module orders.

names.note: Lasers and modules. Broad end-market mix dilutes the read.
names.watch: Datacenter transceiver bookings vs telecom mix.

names.note: Contract manufacturer. Concentration is the whole risk.
names.watch: Top-customer concentration and optical-module volumes.

names.note: Small, volatile, single-customer sensitive.
names.watch: Single-customer order timing — very lumpy.

names.note: Laser supply into module makers.
names.watch: Cloud/datacenter laser bookings and channel inventory.

layers.name: Signal & connectivity chips
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Design wins lock in years of revenue.

names.note: Concentration is the single most important fact here.
names.watch: Top-2 buyer concentration and AEC/DSP ramp.

names.note: Connectivity silicon, rack-scale.
names.watch: Rack-scale connectivity design wins with hyperscalers.

layers.name: Switching & networking
layers.lagText: Three quarters. Follows rack deployment, not order books.

names.note: Cleanest listed read on datacenter fabric.
names.watch: Cloud-titan switching orders and backlog.

names.note: DCI and long-haul. Telco mix slows the read-through.
names.watch: Datacenter-interconnect mix vs telco carrier spend.

layers.name: Power, cooling & capacity
layers.lagText: Four quarters. Physical buildout. Slowest and stickiest.

names.note: Datacenter thermal and power systems — a direct AI-buildout beneficiary.
names.watch: Order book and backlog — the leading indicator.

names.note: Broad industrial base dilutes AI exposure.
names.watch: Datacenter electrical backlog vs the broad industrial mix.

names.note: Neocloud HPC-datacenter operator — a capacity play, not a chipmaker.
names.watch: Financing terms and contracted capacity — not just demand.

names.note: GPU-capacity reseller — effectively an AI-compute landlord.
names.watch: Contract length and GPU-capacity utilization.

theses.how: Each company's share = its trailing revenue × an estimated 'AI-attributable' fraction (its exposure band: high / moderate / low), divided by the chain total. So it answers who actually captures the spend TODAY — not who might benefit next. Revenue is live from our scan; a few names our universe doesn't cover use a flagged revenue estimate. Exposure bands are qualitative judgements from filings and earnings calls, and they are the part most worth arguing with. This is a snapshot of realized share, not a prediction — later position in the chain does NOT imply un-captured upside; markets price expectations ahead, and many of these names have already run. The 'signal to watch' is the single leading indicator we'd track for each name.
theses.disclaimer: This is a factual map of supply chain relationships. It is not investment advice, not a recommendation to buy or sell any security, and nothing here accounts for your circumstances. Company classifications change; verify against primary filings before acting.

theses.title: The power build-out behind the AI boom
theses.standfirst: AI datacenters and electrification are colliding with a grid that took decades to build. This map shows where the power-build dollar has already landed — each layer's and each company's share of the revenue the chain captures today, weighted by how much of that business depends on the build-out. Descriptive, not a forecast.

control.label: US electricity / power-capex growth, year over year

market.note: Rough estimates of US power-system investment (grid, generation, interconnection) driven by AI + electrification — our read as of mid-2026, not a precise figure.

layers.name: Generation — turbines & nuclear
layers.lagText: First to feel it. Long-lead equipment and firm-power contracts.

names.note: Gas turbines booked years out — the cleanest pick-and-shovel on power demand.
names.watch: Gas-turbine slot bookings into 2028 and grid orders.

names.note: Largest US nuclear fleet; direct power deals with hyperscalers re-rate it.
names.watch: Behind-the-meter / PPA deals with hyperscalers and uprates.

names.note: Merchant generation; load growth lifts the whole fleet's economics.
names.watch: Merchant power prices and data-center PPA signings.

layers.name: Grid — transformers & switchgear
layers.lagText: About one quarter behind. Backlogs stretched, lead times long.

names.note: Electrical backbone for datacenters and the grid. Also appears in the AI Capex chain.
names.watch: Datacenter + grid electrical backlog.

names.note: Utility transmission & distribution gear — grid capex flows straight through.
names.watch: Utility T&D order rates and grid-hardening spend.

names.note: Switchgear with very long lead times; backlog is the tell.
names.watch: Switchgear backlog and lead-time commentary.

layers.name: Components, conduit & cable
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Commoditised, so price and volume both matter.

names.note: Enclosures, connections and liquid-cooling plumbing.
names.watch: Liquid-cooling and connection attach into datacenters.

names.note: Electrical conduit — high volume, but price-cyclical.
names.watch: Conduit volume vs price (steel/PVC cycle).

layers.name: EPC & grid construction
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Multi-year backlogs convert slowly but stick.

names.note: The grid's contractor. Multi-year backlog is the leading indicator.
names.watch: Multi-year utility/grid backlog and book-to-bill.

names.note: Transmission & distribution construction — a purer grid read than the diversifieds.
names.watch: T&D construction backlog.

names.note: Energy and utility EPC; mixed end-markets dilute the signal.
names.watch: Utility + energy segment book-to-bill.

names.note: Broad infrastructure base; power is a growing but not sole driver.
names.watch: Power-delivery segment growth within the mix.

layers.name: Cooling & rack thermal
layers.lagText: Three quarters. The last mile of the electron — and the AI chain's L6.

names.note: Thermal and power management at the rack. Cross-listed in the AI Capex chain.
names.watch: Backlog (thermal + power management).

names.note: Backup power; datacenter is a small but growing slice of a consumer-heavy base.
names.watch: Datacenter/industrial mix vs consumer standby demand.

theses.how: Layers are ordered by where the money arrives first. The lag is the typical delay between power demand firming up and that spend landing in a supplier's revenue. Some names — Eaton, Vertiv — sit in both this map and the AI Capex chain, because AI is the loudest single driver of the power build-out. Exposure bands are qualitative judgements from filings and calls, and they are the part most worth arguing with.
theses.disclaimer: This is a factual map of supply chain relationships. It is not investment advice, not a recommendation to buy or sell any security, and nothing here accounts for your circumstances. Company classifications change; verify against primary filings before acting.

Descriptive, not a forecast.

control.label: US defense outlays growth, year over year

market.note: Round figures for the US defense budget and its investment (procurement + R&D) slice — recurring annual outlays, not a one-time prize. Our read, mid-2026.

layers.name: Prime contractors
layers.lagText: Booked first as programs of record. Backlog is deep and slow.

names.note: The bellwether prime; missiles and aeronautics anchor the backlog.
names.watch: Book-to-bill and missile / aeronautics backlog.

names.note: Levered to strategic programs — B-21 and Sentinel.
names.watch: B-21 and Sentinel program cadence.

names.watch: Raytheon defense backlog vs commercial-aero recovery.

layers.name: Electronics, sensors & C4ISR
layers.lagText: About a quarter behind the primes; content per platform is rising.

names.note: Resilient comms, EW and munitions — a merchant-supplier prime.
names.watch: Munitions restocking and resilient-comms orders.

names.note: Sub-tier defense electronics; orders are lumpy and program-timed.
names.watch: Book-to-bill in defense electronics (very lumpy).

names.note: IT and systems integration; funded backlog converts steadily.
names.watch: Contract awards and backlog conversion.

layers.name: Drones & autonomy
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Fast-growing, but small bases and single-program risk.

names.note: Target drones, tactical systems and propulsion. High beta to program wins.
names.watch: Drone / target-system awards and tactical-missile progress.

names.note: Loitering munitions and small UAS; international demand is the swing.
names.watch: Switchblade + international loitering-munition demand.

layers.name: IT, cyber & services
layers.lagText: Two quarters. Steady, labour-based, recompete-driven.

names.note: Advisory and digital services; funded backlog is the tell.
names.watch: Book-to-bill and funded backlog.

names.note: Technology and expertise contracts; recompete win-rate matters.
names.watch: Awards and recompete win rate.

names.note: Systems integration; a slower, steadier read on outlays.
names.watch: Backlog and book-to-bill.

layers.name: Shipbuilding & heavy
layers.lagText: Three quarters-plus. The longest cycle and the tightest labour.

names.note: The pure-play Navy shipbuilder; throughput and labour are the constraint.
names.watch: Navy shipbuilding backlog and labour / throughput.

names.note: Electric Boat submarines — cross-listed with the primes.
names.watch: Submarine (Electric Boat) build cadence.

theses.how: Layers are ordered by where an outlay increase lands first — programs of record at the primes, then the content-rich electronics, the fast-growing autonomy names, the labour-based services, and the very long shipbuilding cycle last. Defense orders are lumpy and program-timed, so the lag here is looser than in a commercial capex chain. Exposure bands are qualitative judgements from filings; the note also flags that some capability (e.g. Anduril in autonomy) sits in private hands and is not investable here.

layers.name: Materials & inputs
layers.lagText: Two quarters, then sticky. Local, heavy and priced by the truckload.

theses.how: Layers are ordered by where the build-out money lands first — the fab tools ordered before the building is finished, then automation, the mechanical and electrical contractors, and finally the heavy materials trucked to the site. Exposure bands are qualitative judgements from filings and calls.

theses.title: Where the obesity-drug dollar lands
theses.standfirst: The GLP-1 wave is one of the fastest-growing markets in pharma history. This map shows where the obesity-drug dollar has already landed — each layer's and each company's share of the GLP-1 revenue the chain captures today: the drugmakers, the supply and CDMO layer, the delivery devices, and the adjacent beneficiaries.

market.note: Rough estimates of the GLP-1 / anti-obesity value chain, our read as of mid-2026 — meant to be argued with.

names.note: Zepbound/Mounjaro (tirzepatide) — the share leader by growth.
names.watch: Incretin revenue, supply, and oral (orforglipron) data.

names.note: Wegovy/Ozempic (semaglutide) — the co-leader (ADR).
names.watch: Wegovy supply/scripts and CagriSema readouts.

names.note: MariTide — a later-stage challenger with monthly dosing.
names.watch: MariTide Phase 3 data and dosing profile.

names.note: Clinical-stage (VK2735) — pure optionality, pre-revenue.

names.note: Elastomer containment plus self-injection pen/auto-injector components — the purest 'picks-and-shovels' on injectable GLP-1s.
